provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: New term new choices
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state their new goals for the term
The pupils should be able to list three good character traits
Introduction:
We are back to school after a long holiday
We can make good choices this term
Content:
A goal is something we want to do
We can set small goals like being kind or honest
Kind means being nice to others
Honest means telling the truth
Hardworking means trying our best
Class activity:
Each child will draw one picture showing a good choice
Evaluation questions:
What is a goal?
Name one good character trait
How can you be kind today?
Summary:
We can all make good choices to be better children

topics.title: The golden rule
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain the golden rule
The pupils should be able to demonstrate the golden rule
Introduction:
We all like when people are nice to us
The golden rule teaches us how to treat others
Content:
The golden rule says do to others what you love
If you love to be helped, help others
If you love to share, share with others
We can show love by sharing toys or helping friends
Class activity:
Children will work in pairs to take turns helping each other
Evaluation questions:
What is the golden rule?
How can you show the golden rule?
What happens when we follow the golden rule?
Summary:
The golden rule helps us love others like we want to be loved

topics.title: Respect for the flag
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify the Nigerian flag
The pupils should be able to show respect for the flag
Introduction:
Our country is Nigeria
We show respect for our country with the flag
Content:
The Nigerian flag has green white green
Green stands for our good land
White stands for peace
When we see the flag, we stand quietly
We sing the national anthem with respect
Class activity:
Children will practice standing still when the flag is shown
Evaluation questions:
What colours are on our flag?
What do we do when we see the flag?
Why do we respect the flag?
Summary:
The flag represents our country and we must always respect it

topics.title: Telling the truth
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tell the difference between truth and lie
The pupils should be able to explain why truth builds trust
Introduction:
Sometimes we want to hide mistakes
But telling the truth is always best
Content:
The truth is what really happened
A lie is saying something that is not true
When we tell the truth, people trust us
Trust means believing what someone says
Class activity:
Children will tell one true thing about themselves
Evaluation questions:
What is the truth?
Why should we always tell the truth?
What happens when people tell lies?
Summary:
Telling the truth helps us build trust with others

topics.title: No stealing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain why stealing is wrong
The pupils should be able to list ways to avoid stealing
Introduction:
Sometimes we want things that belong to others
Taking things without asking is stealing
Content:
Stealing is taking what is not ours
We must always ask before taking something
If we borrow something, we must return it
Taking things without permission hurts others
Class activity:
Children will practice asking to borrow classroom items
Evaluation questions:
What is stealing?
What should we do before taking something?
Why is stealing wrong?
Summary:
We must always respect other people's things

topics.title: Cleanliness
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list ways to stay clean
The pupils should be able to explain why cleanliness is important
Introduction:
We all like to be clean and fresh
Cleanliness helps us stay healthy
Content:
We must wash our hands with soap
We must keep our bodies clean with bath
We must keep our rooms tidy
Cleaning our things shows we care for them
Class activity:
Children will practice cleaning their small toys
Evaluation questions:
Why do we need to be clean?
Name one way to keep your body clean
What happens if we don't keep clean?
Summary:
Cleanliness is a good habit that keeps us healthy

topics.title: Obedience brings peace
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify people to obey
The pupils should be able to explain the benefits of obedience
Introduction:
We have many people who guide us
Listening to them keeps us safe and happy
Content:
We must obey our parents at home
We must obey our teachers at school
We must obey older people
Obeying the first time makes things easy for everyone
Class activity:
Children will practice obeying instructions the first time
Evaluation questions:
Who should we obey?
What happens when we obey quickly?
Why is obedience important?
Summary:
Obedience brings peace and makes everyone happy

topics.title: Forgiving friends
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain what forgiveness means
The pupils should be able to demonstrate forgiveness
Introduction:
Sometimes friends hurt us by mistake
Forgiving helps us stay friends
Content:
Forgiveness means letting go of bad feelings
When we forgive, we choose to be happy again
We should forgive quickly to keep peace
Forgiving helps us feel free inside
Class activity:
Children will practice saying I forgive you to a friend
Evaluation questions:
What is forgiveness?
Why should we forgive friends?
How do you feel after forgiving someone?
Summary:
Forgiving helps us stay happy with our friends

topics.title: Gratitude to God
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list things to thank God for
The pupils should be able to show gratitude
Introduction:
God gives us many good things every day
We should always say thank you
Content:
We thank God for our family who loves us
We thank God for food to eat
We thank God for school to learn
We can count our blessings every day
Class activity:
Children will draw one thing they are thankful for
Evaluation questions:
What are you thankful for today?
Why should we thank God?
How can we show we are grateful?
Summary:
We should always be thankful for God's good gifts

topics.title: Revision and character awards
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite the rules learned
The pupils should be able to identify good character traits
Introduction:
We have learned many good things this term
Today we celebrate our good choices
Content:
We will remember to be kind and honest
We will remember to respect our flag and tell truth
We will remember to be clean and obedient
We will remember to forgive and be thankful
Class activity:
Children will share their best character choice this term
Evaluation questions:
What is one rule you learned this term?
How have you been kind to others?
Why is it good to make good choices?
Summary:
Today we celebrate all the good children in our class
